citations.claim: total energy at first violating step has drifted far from initial value
bodies have fallen to very close separation with high speed at violation
energy still conserved one step before violation during close infall

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.0287169 to 0.001 keeping all else identical; finer integration removes the energy drift

explanation: Two heavy bodies start at rest and fall head-on toward each other. By step 13 separation is ~0.91 with speed ~7, by step 14 separation is ~0.43 with speed ~10.2. The fixed-dt leapfrog with only 16 substeps in the final step cannot resolve the rapidly deepening softened potential (potential ~ -2153, kinetic ~1619), so integration error injects ~116 energy drift, exceeding the 2% allowance. Reducing dt to 0.001 eliminates the violation, confirming coarse time resolution during deep close approach as cause.
vision_note: Two blue bodies in the upper-left corner fall directly toward each other through steps 11 to 13 and nearly coincide by step 14. The rapid head-on close approach ends in overlap with elongated velocity trails.
